findings.summary: The wrapper's way of finding the subcommand is not specified or shared, so `cargo -q build` or `cargo --locked test` can run with no slot, and no test catches it.
findings.evidence: check_cargo skips leading global flags (-q, --quiet, -v, -vv, --verbose, --locked, --offline, --frozen) before reading the subcommand, so the policy allows `cargo --locked test`. Plan step 4 requires the wrapper for `cargo -q build`. Step 2 adds `cargo_subcommand` as a private function in policy.rs; only `slotted_cargo_commands` is public. Step 3 says the wrapper passes 'a non-slotted subcommand' through, without saying how it parses one. Decision 7 shares only BUILD_SLOT_SUBCOMMANDS and takes_build_slot. Criterion 1 test (b) uses only `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy`, `check` and `fmt --check`, so a wrapper that reads only args[0] would pass every test while `cargo -q build` passes through unslotted. That breaks criterion 1 for an allowed form. Fix: Make `cargo_subcommand` (skipping leading dash words the way check_cargo does) public in athena-agent lib.rs, and use it in cargo_wrapper, the policy and slotted_cargo_commands. Add `cargo -q build` and `cargo --locked test` to criterion 1 test (b): each must hold the slot while it runs and write a `ran` log line.

findings.summary: The hook checks its own PATH, not the PATH the Bash tool actually uses; a mismatch is only detected after the fact.
findings.evidence: BuildWrapper::from_env reads PATH from the hook process (hooks.rs:52-67). Claude Code's Bash tool may rebuild PATH from a shell snapshot, since HOME is passed (athena.toml:52). The plan admits this and relies on the status note to show it. Decision 1 rejected rewriting the command in the hook ('needs new hook output'). But a PreToolUse rewrite to the wrapper's full path (`<dir>/cargo ...`) would make the guarantee independent of PATH, and the program word stays `cargo`-shaped for the seen-count. Fix: Either weigh a hook rewrite to the wrapper's full path as the enforcement point (the PATH wrapper stays for nested use), or state in the Built note that the policy rule covers the hook's PATH only, and mark it prose-only per the mechanism default.

findings.summary: The 'job not failed' half of the test cannot fail without the feature; only the build_slots assertion can.
findings.evidence: invoke_and_record (invocation.rs:230-263) returns Ok whatever is in the log, so 'returns Ok with outcome unchanged' holds even without the change. The plan says this openly and calls the rest a design argument. Fix: Keep the test, but name its 'Fails without' line as the build_slots assertion only. Mark 'job not failed' as a design argument (prose-only) in the criterion 3 demonstration and the Built note.

findings.summary: The peak is counted only when a producer command wins a slot; design step 4 says the queue records the peak.
findings.evidence: agent-and-build-slots.md:411 says 'the peak number of slots held at once, which the queue records'. Slot::held() is sampled only after a producer wins, so peaks made by checks alone are never seen. The plan labels it a lower bound. Fix: Keep the label. Also record `Slot::held()` on the check side's existing queued_s path if that can be done without touching step-3 files; otherwise state the gap explicitly in the Built note (it does).

pr_check.rs literal is at 269 (plan says ~320), reconcile.rs at 245 (~296), landing_tests.rs at 125 (~167); landing_tests.rs:1487 calls the helper and is not a literal. Fix: Update the line references; the compiler will find any missed literal anyway.

summary: I read the code the plan names and checked its main claims. Most hold: SlotQueue::acquire/try_acquire/waiting/from_config, Class::Producer = 2, the flock-based slot files, the pre-commit/commit-msg dispatch at main.rs:551, policy.rs evaluate/check_bash/check_segment/check_cargo/tokenize and the `bash` helper at 991, invocation.rs invoke_and_record (the Invocation literal is in invocation_record at 195, plus interrupted_record at 281), reading.rs agent_spec with `side`, and procs kill_group/group_alive. Only run/producer.rs:166 passes Side::Produce, and every Policy literal outside policy.rs is a verifier policy, including tests/binary.rs:98. I found no reader of the changed code that the dependents list leaves out. The six 'outside the deliverables' findings in the brief are explained in decision 17: each file is either the only place that can do the job or a one-line edit needed to compile. One major gap: the policy lets the producer put global flags before the subcommand (`cargo -q build`, `cargo --locked test`; CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS at policy.rs:477-486), and the plan's own policy rule requires the wrapper for `cargo -q build`. But the plan never says how the wrapper finds the subcommand. `cargo_subcommand` is added to policy.rs as a private function, and the criterion 1 tests use only bare `cargo build/test/clippy/check`. A wrapper that looks only at its first argument would run these common forms with no slot, and no test would catch it. Three minor points: the hook checks its own PATH, not the one the Bash tool uses; the 'not failed' test cannot fail without the feature; and the peak is only sampled when a producer command wins a slot. Line references to three Invocation literals are slightly off (nit). Verdict: revise.
